historical_references.reference: Ibn Khaldun's 'Al-'Ibar: An Autobiography', translated by Franz Rosenthal. New York: New York University Press, 1958.
historical_references.context: The name Bakirin is mentioned in relation to the Berber Banu Ghana dynasty, which ruled over the trans-Saharan trade region. Ibn Khaldun describes Bakirin as the chief of the Banu Ghana and the founder of the city of Ghanqa (Ghana) in the Fezzan region.

historical_references.reference: Al-Bakri, Ihya Ibn Abd al-Hakam. The Muqaddimah of Ibn Khaldun: A Fragment. Translated by Roslane Schomberg. Leiden: Brill, 1967.
historical_references.context: In Al-Bakri's geographical work 'Al-Maslik wa Al-Mamalik', the name Bakirin is mentioned as the chief of the Berber tribe of Banu Hilal, who migrated from the Nafusa Mountains to the Fezzan region in the 11th century. This migration led to the establishment of the Hawwara state in Fezzan.
